chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: Running Wild, Cecil Mack and an early record with a choir
summary: She remembers Running Wild and recalls making one of the first records with a choir behind singer Elkins, probably for Black Swan.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: It was Cecil Mack and Johnny Johnston Jones who introduced the Charleston in Running Wild, a show called Running Wild.

Uh-huh, well, Running -- yes, I remember Running Wild well. Let me see. Cecil Mack, you know, collaborated with Eubie Blake in writing a lot of his music, because he wrote -- oh, I remember the first record that was made with a choir. I made it with a fellow named Elkins, and he had a big choir behind him.
And I made -- what was that thing that Cecil Mack wrote? Lord, have mercy, what was that thing?

See, it was during the time of -- it was either Shuffle Along or Running Wild. It was during that time. And I made it with Elkins, with a choir, and I think that was for Paramount. It was either for Paramount or the Black Swan. No, it was the Black Swan, I believe.
